differences.what: Exposure of the white carton: B shows the front face as white (luma 232-238 below the label, label paper 250), while A sits at 204-210 with label paper at 224, so A's product reads light grey and dingy at any size, the most visible problem in either frame
White ink on the red base: B's SHAKE WELL reads as white (RGB about 243-248), while A's reads as grey (about 200-205)

Printed type: B's logo and Nutrition Facts panel are crisper, true black on white (type p5 luma 0 vs 25 in A). A's type is soft and greyed. Letterforms are identical in both, so B's processing did not distort the type

Set tone: B lifts the sweep by about 10-16 levels (wall 107-128, floor 130-144, against A's 97-115 and 116-128), so the set reads cleaner and airier where A's is murky. Product-to-wall separation ratio is the same in both

Highlight clipping: B's tone shoulder blows out the top of the front face around the logo (5,267 px at >=253 in all channels) and much of the label paper (2,613 px). This flattens the face's modelling and loses the bevel line under the eave, and in print those areas would carry no ink. A keeps full gradation: the face peaks at 246 and nothing on the product clips

Sharpening halos: B has 1-px unsharp-mask halos at the silhouette, +3.6 bright and -5 dark at the front face's right edge against the wall, and a -6.4 dark dip at the left edge (A: -2). A's edges are clean
Back-panel status LED: A keeps it cyan (core RGB 200,255,255), while B blows it to pure white (255,255,255) and the colour is lost
Grain on the sweep: B's sharpening raises fine noise by about 40% (high-pass std 0.53 vs 0.38). Both are still very clean, so this is minor
